title: security: rbac-v2 + KMS region pinning enforcement + audit logging hardening
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: tighten RBAC v2 enforcement for KMS-backed keys and ensure data-residency (region pinning) policies are auditable and enforced across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. This PR implements validation and enforcement hooks in the RBAC layer to prevent mismatched KMS region assignments, enhances audit logging for all KMS operations, and introduces a migration + feature flag for gradual rollout.

What this PR does: - Adds KMS region pinning checks to the RBAC v2 policy evaluator (rejects writes/creates that would attach a key outside the allowed residency set) - Emits structured audit events on KMS key usage, rotation, and policy changes (includes before/after snapshots, actor, request_id, and residency tags) - Introduces a residency whitelist configuration and an enforcer mode toggle (audit-only | enforce) for orgs to test before full enforcement - Adds CLI migration to backfill existing keys and annotate resources with residency metadata - Adds server-side integration tests and unit coverage for new evaluator logic - Updates docs and console feature flag UI strings for operators and security teams

Rollout plan: staged rollout starting with audit-only mode for 2 weeks, enable enforcement for orgs on allowlist, monitor alerts/metrics (new metric: rbac.kms.region_pin.rejections) before global enforcement. Linear/SEC tickets referenced.

Backward compatibility: default is audit-only, so no immediate breaks for existing customers. Enforcement requires opt-in via console flag or org-level config.

Migration: includes a safe backfill that tags keys with inferred region based on account metadata; migration is idempotent and reversible.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Migration script and dry-run - [x] Security review - [x] Docs updated

Related: ENG-5421 for policy evaluator refactor, SUP-1123 for customer support case that motivated stricter enforcement.
